tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- Prefer the Edit tool for modifying existing files — it only sends the diff. Only use this tool to create new files or for complete rewrites.
- NEVER create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

1	# Implementation Plan: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
2	
3	**Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
4	extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)
5	
6	**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
7	
8	**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/011-settings-dashboard/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
9	§1 (RF09), §4 (RNF05), §6.6–6.7 (`dashboard-aggregate-get`/`dashboard-narrative-get`/`account-settings-update`/
10	`account-delete`), §6.1 (`auth-logout`), §8 (data model reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/
11	openapi.yaml`'s `/dashboard/*`, `/account*`, `/auth/logout` schemas; `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s
12	function-name mapping; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`
13	§2.6, §6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on F000 (session, login, routing) and RF01 (entries
14	exist to aggregate), both already implemented. This is the unit that replaces `SettingsPlaceholderPage` (the
15	route `AppRoutes.settings` already points at a static "Ainda não disponível." placeholder) with the real
16	screen, and that finally wires in the real display name `app_drawer.dart`'s own stand-in email-derivation
17	comment has been waiting for since F000.
18	
19	## Summary
20	
21	The Settings screen (`AppRoutes.settings`, currently `SettingsPlaceholderPage`) becomes a real, four-concern
22	screen backed by one screen-scoped `SettingsBloc`: (1) an evolution dashboard — `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and
23	`GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, the aggregate's ten-bar chart built by a new pure
24	derivation (`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`, research.md R2) and rendered with plain `Container`-based bars
25	(no new charting dependency, research.md R3); (2) an editable profile header (52px initials avatar, inline
26	pencil-to-check name editing via `PATCH /account/settings`, read-only email) backed by a new, narrow
27	`AccountProfileRepository` whose confirmed writes persist into a new `AccountProfileLocalCache`
28	(`features/settings/data/`, Keychain-backed) — the one local mirror this unit adds, since no earlier unit
29	ever wrote `displayName`; (3) a biometrics toggle that is hidden entirely on a device with no usable
30	capability and otherwise reuses RF03's own `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`VaultRepository` as-is behind a
31	new, settings-owned, await-then-revert usecase (research.md R6) rather than RF03's deliberately
32	fire-and-forget one; (4) "Sair" (extends the existing `AuthRepository` with one new method, `logout()`) and
33	"Apagar conta" (a new `AccountDeletionRepository`, `DELETE /account`), both ending in the same
34	clear-local-state-and-navigate sequence spec.md's own Assumptions resolve to the existing vault/login routes
35	(research.md R10) — deletion alone additionally wipes `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` (both extended in
36	place with a new `clear()` method) since "any other locally held user data" (FR-019) is a strictly wider
37	clear than logout's own FR-016 wording. `app_drawer.dart` is extended in place to read the same cached display
38	name (research.md R13), and `SettingsPage` becomes `RouteAware` on the already-existing `chatRouteObserver` so
39	re-authenticating mid-screen re-requests fresh data rather than only preserving stale state (research.md R15).
40	
41	## Technical Context
42	
43	**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from every prior
44	unit.
45	
46	**Primary Dependencies**: None added. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
47	`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, no new method needed — every call here is a plain JSON `call()`, the same
48	shape `BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource` already uses), `flutter_secure_storage` (via a new
49	`AccountProfileLocalCache`, same pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`/`EntriesLocalCache`), `local_auth` (indirectly,
50	through the unmodified `VaultRepository`), `go_router` (no new route — `AppRoutes.settings` already exists;
51	only its builder changes); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`. Research.md R3 explicitly rejects adding a
52	charting package — the 10-bar chart is plain `Container`s.
53	
54	**Storage**: One new on-device key, `AccountProfileLocalCache`'s single `settingsDisplayName` Keychain entry
55	(research.md R5/R7) — the only new local persistence this unit introduces. `DashboardAggregate`/
56	`DashboardNarrative` are explicitly never persisted (FR-008 — "recomputed fresh... never served from a result
57	cached from a previous visit"), unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`'s own cross-restart caches.
58	
59	**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
60	--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising
61	`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`'s pure bucketing (research.md R2 — the single richest piece of new domain
62	logic this unit adds, mirroring `DateRangeFilter`/`SyncBadgeState`'s existing pure-derivation test shape),
63	`AccountProfile.isValidDisplayName`/`.initials`/`.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail`, and
64	`SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`'s await-then-mirror-or-revert branches (contracts/
65	biometric-preference-settings-extension.md) against `mocktail` fakes of `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/
66	`VaultRepository` — no new fakes needed for `local_auth`/`flutter_secure_storage` themselves, since neither is
67	touched directly by anything new.
68	
69	**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched; no new package needs an
70	iOS install step.
71	
72	**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/settings/`
73	(domain/data/presentation, Principle V) replacing the one-file `SettingsPlaceholderPage` (deleted); three
74	existing files extended in place — `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart` (+
75	`data`/`impl`, + `logout()`), `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` (+ `impl`, +
76	`clearLocalData()`), `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart` (+ `impl`, +
77	`clearLocalData()`) — plus their respective local caches (`EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`) each gaining a
78	new `clear()` method; `lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart` (display-name read, research.md
79	R13); `lib/core/routing/app_router.dart` (`AppRoutes.settings`'s builder); `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (5 new
80	tokens, research.md R14); `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No backend/server code, no change to
81	`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.
82	
83	**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The optimistic UI flips this unit adds — the biometric toggle's
84	immediate visual change before its network write resolves, and the name field's immediate return to display
85	mode is deliberately *not* optimistic (it waits for the `Right`, since a wrong optimistic name could be shown
86	then silently reverted, worse than a brief wait) — reflect within 100ms where used; every network call in
87	this unit's flow (dashboard load, name save, toggle save, sign-out, deletion) already has a loading indicator
88	by construction (`dashboardStatus == loading`, `nameEditStatus == saving`, `biometricSaving`, `isSigningOut`,
89	`isDeletingAccount` each drive one), satisfying the >300ms affordance requirement.
90	
91	**Constraints**:
92	- No period-switching UI control (FR-002) — the dashboard always requests the fixed `period=all`.
93	- No AI persona selector or any other extension feature (FR-015) — `account-settings-update`'s `persona`
94	  field is never sent by this unit's requests and never read from its responses.
95	- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF09 in the build order, and no backend/contract/config
96	  change (FR-024) — every endpoint this unit calls is one `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already
97	  documents, called exactly as documented (contracts/*.md's own request-shape listings).
98	- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `settings/domain/` imports only `equatable`/
99	  `fpdart`/`core/network/failure.dart`; `SettingsBloc` depends on `settings/domain/` repositories/usecases plus
100	  two other features' already-domain-layer interfaces (`vault/domain/`'s `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/
101	  `VaultRepository`, `auth/domain/`'s `AuthRepository`, `session/domain/`'s `SessionRepository`,
102	  `entries/domain/`'s `EntriesRepository`, `chat/domain/`'s `ChatRepository`) — never any other feature's
103	  `presentation/bloc/` (enforced by `test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`, unmodified, which
104	  already scans every `presentation/bloc/` path recursively).
105	- FR-022's concurrency guard is satisfied by `SettingsState`'s own `isSigningOut`/`isDeletingAccount` booleans
106	  (research.md R12), not a shared/persisted flag — the same shape `ExportBloc`'s own tap-guard already uses.
107	- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — the 5 genuinely
108	  new values this unit needs (data-model.md's token table, research.md R14) are added there, not inlined.
109	
110	**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`settings/`) with 4 domain entities + 1 pure bucketing extension, 3
111	repository interfaces + 1 reused usecase pattern (1 new settings-owned usecase), 3 data classes (2 remote data
112	sources + 1 local cache) + 3 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), ~7 new presentation widgets; 3
113	existing features' interfaces each extended by exactly one method (+ impl); 2 existing local caches each
114	gaining a `clear()` method; 1 existing widget (`app_drawer.dart`) extended in place; 1 deleted file
115	(`settings_placeholder_page.dart`); 5 new `DesignTokens` values; ~14 new DI registrations.
116	
117	## Constitution Check
118	
119	*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*
120	
121	| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
122	|---|---|---|
123	| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. Every technical-judgment decision this plan makes (R1–R16, research.md) is built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Clarifications/Assumptions/Edge-Cases wording — the data-flow split (R1), the bucketing arithmetic (R2), the no-new-dependency chart (R3), the flat composite state shape (R4), the per-field caching split (R5), the biometric await-revert usecase (R6), the narrow display-name repository (R7), the logout/deletion homing (R8), the clear-scope split (R9), the post-action destination (R10), the reauth-stream wiring (R11), the concurrency guards (R12), the extracted email-derivation (R13), the 5 new tokens (R14), the `RouteAware` post-reauth refresh (R15) — none reopens a resolved Clarification. |
124	| II. Fixed Technology Stack | PASS | No change to `flutter_bloc`/`fpdart`/`get_it`/Clean Architecture. Zero new dependencies (research.md R3) — the first unit in the delivery order to need no pubspec addition at all. |
125	| III. Backend Boundary | PASS | Only already-contracted functions called (`dashboard-aggregate-get`, `dashboard-narrative-get`, `account-settings-update`, `account-delete`, `auth-logout` — `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s own path→function table); no AI provider called directly (the narrative's Claude Haiku 4.5 generation stays entirely server-side, consumed only as the already-generated `text` field). `account-delete`'s `confirmation: "DELETE"` value is supplied by the app itself, never collected from the user as free text — no new surface for a credential/secret to leak through. |
126	| IV. Design Token Discipline & Visual Fidelity | PASS | 5 new `DesignTokens` values (research.md R14/data-model.md), each traceable to either the prototype's own stated dimension (`sizeAvatarSettings = 52`, prototype-extract.md §6) or a reasonable, narrowly-scoped new value where the prototype's token panel is silent on chart geometry — never an inline literal in a widget file. UI text — "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui," "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.," "Apagar sua conta?," "Apagar tudo," "Cancelar," "Sair," "Apagar conta" — is exactly as spec.md's own FR/Acceptance-Scenario wording and prototype-extract.md §2.6 state it, in Portuguese; the one new copy this unit must author itself (the "narrativa indisponível" message's exact sentence, since the prototype names the state but not its literal string) is written in Portuguese consistent with the rest of the screen's register. |
127	| V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention | PASS | `settings/domain/` imports only `equatable`/`fpdart`/`core/network/failure.dart` — confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart` (unmodified, scans recursively). `SettingsBloc`'s dependency surface is exactly the repository/usecase interfaces listed in Technical Context's own Constraints entry — no other feature's `presentation/bloc/` import (confirmed against `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`, unmodified). |
128	| RNF01 (latency) | PASS | See Technical Context's own Performance Goals entry — every network call in this unit's flow already shows a loading indicator by construction; the two deliberately-optimistic flips (biometric toggle) reflect in well under 100ms, the two deliberately-non-optimistic ones (name save, sign-out/deletion's final navigation) wait for a confirmed result by design, not by omission. |
129	| RNF02/03/04 (PII, retention, RLS) | N/A to RF09 | Backend-side; this unit sends no new PII-bearing content (a display name and a boolean are the only new request bodies) and introduces no new on-device retention beyond the one Keychain key already covered under Storage above. |
130	| RNF05 (hard delete) | PASS | This is the unit RNF05 names explicitly — `DELETE /account` is exposed from Settings exactly as required, gated behind the prototype's own two-button confirmation dialog (FR-017/FR-018), with the app-side local-data clear (research.md R9) going beyond the backend's own cascade to also remove every on-device trace this app itself holds. |
131	| RNF06 (layer violations) | PASS | No `settings/domain/` file imports Flutter or a `settings/data/` class; `SettingsBloc` imports no other feature's `presentation/bloc/` path — both mechanically re-confirmed by the two unmodified architecture tests after this unit's files exist (Post-Design section below). |
132	| RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | `DashboardAggregate.tenBars()` is a pure, total function over `(buckets, today)` with zero I/O (research.md R2) — as directly testable as `DateRangeFilter`/`SyncBadgeState`; `AccountProfile`'s three pure helpers and `SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`'s branches are equally testable against `mocktail` fakes, same shape as every prior unit's own domain coverage. |
133	| RNF08 (visual fidelity) | PASS | Every state matches prototype-extract.md §2.6's own four named dashboard variations plus the confirmation dialog's own described layout — no approximated layout or invented component beyond what spec.md/the prototype already name (the "narrativa indisponível" message's exact wording is the one genuinely new copy, same as RF05's own one new "erroCompleto" string had to be). |
134	| RNF09 (Either + 15/15 error scenarios) | PASS (gate carried into tasks) | Two new write endpoints (`account-delete`, `auth-logout`) and one extended existing one (`account-settings-update`'s `displayName` body shape, already RF03-counted) each get full timeout/malformed/no-connection coverage per contracts/*.md's own scenario tables (research.md R16) — this plan does not assert a specific final project-wide fraction, consistent with every prior unit's own hedging on that number. |
135	
136	*Post-Phase-1 re-check: see "Post-Design Constitution Check" at the end of this document.*

# Implementation Plan: P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard

**Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's
extension hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-24 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/011-settings-dashboard/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md`
§1 (RF09), §4 (RNF05), §6.6–6.7 (`dashboard-aggregate-get`/`dashboard-narrative-get`/`account-settings-update`/
`account-delete`), §6.1 (`auth-logout`), §8 (data model reference), §9 (stack), §13; `docs/input/backend/api/
openapi.yaml`'s `/dashboard/*`, `/account*`, `/auth/logout` schemas; `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s
function-name mapping; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`
§2.6, §6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on F000 (session, login, routing) and RF01 (entries
exist to aggregate), both already implemented. This is the unit that replaces `SettingsPlaceholderPage` (the
route `AppRoutes.settings` already points at a static "Ainda não disponível." placeholder) with the real
screen, and that finally wires in the real display name `app_drawer.dart`'s own stand-in email-derivation
comment has been waiting for since F000.

## Summary

The Settings screen (`AppRoutes.settings`, currently `SettingsPlaceholderPage`) becomes a real, four-concern
screen backed by one screen-scoped `SettingsBloc`: (1) an evolution dashboard — `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and
`GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, the aggregate's ten-bar chart built by a new pure
derivation (`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`, research.md R2) and rendered with plain `Container`-based bars
(no new charting dependency, research.md R3); (2) an editable profile header (52px initials avatar, inline
pencil-to-check name editing via `PATCH /account/settings`, read-only email) backed by a new, narrow
`AccountProfileRepository` whose confirmed writes persist into a new `AccountProfileLocalCache`
(`features/settings/data/`, Keychain-backed) — the one local mirror this unit adds, since no earlier unit
ever wrote `displayName`; (3) a biometrics toggle that is hidden entirely on a device with no usable
capability and otherwise reuses RF03's own `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/`VaultRepository` as-is behind a
new, settings-owned, await-then-revert usecase (research.md R6) rather than RF03's deliberately
fire-and-forget one; (4) "Sair" (extends the existing `AuthRepository` with one new method, `logout()`) and
"Apagar conta" (a new `AccountDeletionRepository`, `DELETE /account`), both ending in the same
clear-local-state-and-navigate sequence spec.md's own Assumptions resolve to the existing vault/login routes
(research.md R10) — deletion alone additionally wipes `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache` (both extended in
place with a new `clear()` method) since "any other locally held user data" (FR-019) is a strictly wider
clear than logout's own FR-016 wording. `app_drawer.dart` is extended in place to read the same cached display
name (research.md R13), and `SettingsPage` becomes `RouteAware` on the already-existing `chatRouteObserver` so
re-authenticating mid-screen re-requests fresh data rather than only preserving stale state (research.md R15).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from every prior
unit.

**Primary Dependencies**: None added. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, no new method needed — every call here is a plain JSON `call()`, the same
shape `BiometricsPreferenceRemoteDataSource` already uses), `flutter_secure_storage` (via a new
`AccountProfileLocalCache`, same pattern as `VaultSecureStorage`/`EntriesLocalCache`), `local_auth` (indirectly,
through the unmodified `VaultRepository`), `go_router` (no new route — `AppRoutes.settings` already exists;
only its builder changes); dev-only `mocktail`, `bloc_test`. Research.md R3 explicitly rejects adding a
charting package — the 10-bar chart is plain `Container`s.

**Storage**: One new on-device key, `AccountProfileLocalCache`'s single `settingsDisplayName` Keychain entry
(research.md R5/R7) — the only new local persistence this unit introduces. `DashboardAggregate`/
`DashboardNarrative` are explicitly never persisted (FR-008 — "recomputed fresh... never served from a result
cached from a previous visit"), unlike `EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`'s own cross-restart caches.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via `fvm flutter test
--coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising
`DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`'s pure bucketing (research.md R2 — the single richest piece of new domain
logic this unit adds, mirroring `DateRangeFilter`/`SyncBadgeState`'s existing pure-derivation test shape),
`AccountProfile.isValidDisplayName`/`.initials`/`.defaultDisplayNameFromEmail`, and
`SaveSettingsBiometricPreferenceUseCase`'s await-then-mirror-or-revert branches (contracts/
biometric-preference-settings-extension.md) against `mocktail` fakes of `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/
`VaultRepository` — no new fakes needed for `local_auth`/`flutter_secure_storage` themselves, since neither is
touched directly by anything new.

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched; no new package needs an
iOS install step.

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/settings/`
(domain/data/presentation, Principle V) replacing the one-file `SettingsPlaceholderPage` (deleted); three
existing files extended in place — `lib/features/auth/domain/repositories/auth_repository.dart` (+
`data`/`impl`, + `logout()`), `lib/features/entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` (+ `impl`, +
`clearLocalData()`), `lib/features/chat/domain/repositories/chat_repository.dart` (+ `impl`, +
`clearLocalData()`) — plus their respective local caches (`EntriesLocalCache`/`ChatLocalCache`) each gaining a
new `clear()` method; `lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/app_drawer.dart` (display-name read, research.md
R13); `lib/core/routing/app_router.dart` (`AppRoutes.settings`'s builder); `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (5 new
tokens, research.md R14); `lib/core/di/service_locator.dart`. No backend/server code, no change to
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`.

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The optimistic UI flips this unit adds — the biometric toggle's
immediate visual change before its network write resolves, and the name field's immediate return to display
mode is deliberately *not* optimistic (it waits for the `Right`, since a wrong optimistic name could be shown
then silently reverted, worse than a brief wait) — reflect within 100ms where used; every network call in
this unit's flow (dashboard load, name save, toggle save, sign-out, deletion) already has a loading indicator
by construction (`dashboardStatus == loading`, `nameEditStatus == saving`, `biometricSaving`, `isSigningOut`,
`isDeletingAccount` each drive one), satisfying the >300ms affordance requirement.

**Constraints**:
- No period-switching UI control (FR-002) — the dashboard always requests the fixed `period=all`.
- No AI persona selector or any other extension feature (FR-015) — `account-settings-update`'s `persona`
  field is never sent by this unit's requests and never read from its responses.
- No functionality belonging to a unit later than RF09 in the build order, and no backend/contract/config
  change (FR-024) — every endpoint this unit calls is one `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` already
  documents, called exactly as documented (contracts/*.md's own request-shape listings).
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `settings/domain/` imports only `equatable`/
  `fpdart`/`core/network/failure.dart`; `SettingsBloc` depends on `settings/domain/` repositories/usecases plus
  two other features' already-domain-layer interfaces (`vault/domain/`'s `BiometricsPreferenceRepository`/
  `VaultRepository`, `auth/domain/`'s `AuthRepository`, `session/domain/`'s `SessionRepository`,
  `entries/domain/`'s `EntriesRepository`, `chat/domain/`'s `ChatRepository`) — never any other feature's
  `presentation/bloc/` (enforced by `test/architecture/no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`, unmodified, which
  already scans every `presentation/bloc/` path recursively).
- FR-022's concurrency guard is satisfied by `SettingsState`'s own `isSigningOut`/`isDeletingAccount` booleans
  (research.md R12), not a shared/persisted flag — the same shape `ExportBloc`'s own tap-guard already uses.
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — the 5 genuinely
  new values this unit needs (data-model.md's token table, research.md R14) are added there, not inlined.

**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`settings/`) with 4 domain entities + 1 pure bucketing extension, 3
repository interfaces + 1 reused usecase pattern (1 new settings-owned usecase), 3 data classes (2 remote data
sources + 1 local cache) + 3 repository impls, 1 bloc (+events/states), ~7 new presentation widgets; 3
existing features' interfaces each extended by exactly one method (+ impl); 2 existing local caches each
gaining a `clear()` method; 1 existing widget (`app_drawer.dart`) extended in place; 1 deleted file
(`settings_placeholder_page.dart`); 5 new `DesignTokens` values; ~14 new DI registrations.

## Constitution Check

| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. Every technical-judgment decision this plan makes (R1–R16, research.md) is built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Clarifications/Assumptions/Edge-Cases wording — the data-flow split (R1), the bucketing arithmetic (R2), the no-new-dependency chart (R3), the flat composite state shape (R4), the per-field caching split (R5), the biometric await-revert usecase (R6), the narrow display-name repository (R7), the logout/deletion homing (R8), the clear-scope split (R9), the post-action destination (R10), the reauth-stream wiring (R11), the concurrency guards (R12), the extracted email-derivation (R13), the 5 new tokens (R14), the `RouteAware` post-reauth refresh (R15) — none reopens a resolved Clarification. |

## Post-Design Constitution Check

Re-evaluated after Phase 1 (data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md):

- `settings/domain/entities/*.dart` and `settings/domain/repositories/*.dart` were re-checked against their
  actual planned imports: `equatable`, `fpdart` (`Either`/`Unit`), `core/network/failure.dart` only — no
  `package:flutter`, no `settings/data/` class. `domain_purity_test.dart` needs no change to keep covering
  this folder; it already scans every `domain/` path recursively.
- `SettingsBloc`'s dependency surface was re-checked against data-model.md's own repository/usecase list: six
  repository/usecase types, all from `domain/` folders (`settings/`, `vault/`, `auth/`, `session/`,
  `entries/`, `chat/`), zero `presentation/bloc/` imports from any other feature. `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart`
  needs no change either, for the same reason.
- Re-checked that `AuthRepositoryImpl.logout()` does not call `SecureTokenStorage`/`SessionRepository.clear()`
  itself (contracts/account-session-actions.md) — keeping that repository's existing "writes, never deletes"
  shape intact, with the clearing sequence living only in `SettingsBloc`.
- Re-checked that `VaultSecureStorage`'s two existing keys (PIN hash, biometrics-preference mirror) appear in
  no new file's planned write path — `research.md R9`/R10's "deliberately untouched" claim confirmed against
  the actual contracts/account-session-actions.md and contracts/account-deletion-repository.md listings, not
  just asserted.
- Re-checked `DashboardAggregate.tenBars()`'s planned signature: `(List<AggregateBucket>, {DateTime? today})`
  → `List<int>`, zero constructor dependencies, zero I/O — confirmed pure in data-model.md's own listing, the
  one piece of new domain logic RNF07 most needs to hit ≥80% on.
- Re-checked that no change surfaces that touches `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, any native
  iOS project file, or calls an AI provider directly — Principle III remains intact; the narrative's `text`
  field is read and displayed verbatim, never post-processed or evaluated by this app.
- Re-checked `app_drawer.dart`'s planned extension (contracts/app-drawer-display-name-extension.md) against
  Principle V: it depends on `AccountProfileRepository` (a `settings/domain/` interface, resolved via
  `get_it`) and `AccountProfile`'s static helper, never on `AccountProfileLocalCache` (`settings/data/`)
  directly — the same "presentation depends on another feature's domain interface" shape `ChatBloc`'s own
  import of `entries/domain/usecases/create_entry_usecase.dart` already establishes, not a new, unprecedented
  presentation-reaches-into-another-feature's-data shape.

No new violations. Gate remains PASS.

2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `011-settings-dashboard` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-24
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard: Build the Settings screen with the evolution dashboard, and the profile and account actions that live on it. Requirement and acceptance criteria: docs/input/requirements.md, section 1, RF09; RNF05 (section 4) for account deletion. Prototype states: 'Tela 6 — Configurações' in its four dashboard variations and 'Tela 6 — Confirmar exclusão de conta' (prototype extract, section 2.6); profile name editing, 'Sair' and 'Apagar conta'. Backend: GET /dashboard/aggregate, GET /dashboard/narrative, PATCH /account/settings, DELETE /account, POST /auth/logout. Depends on: F000, RF01. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements, section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-24
14	
15	- Q: What should the dashboard show for an account with more than one entry but not yet enough to fill the chart's full set of bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries) — a state the spec's three enumerated scenarios (zero / exactly one / more than thirty) never covered? → A: Render the multi-bar chart using whatever of the ten bars the aggregate's buckets actually populate — naturally partial for a small count — and request the narrative for any count of two or more; "more than thirty" is the seed count chosen to reliably exercise a fully-populated demo chart, not a distinct functional threshold.
16	- Q: For the fixed `all` period, which can span anywhere from a few days to years of history, how should the backend's date-bucketed aggregate be mapped onto the chart's fixed ten bars? → A: Client-side, divide the account's full date range (date of the first entry through today) into ten roughly-equal time slices and sum the backend's per-date counts that fall within each slice to produce each bar's value.
17	- Q: Should the Face ID/Touch ID toggle be hidden entirely or shown-but-disabled on a device with no usable biometric capability? → A: Hidden entirely — the toggle row is omitted from Settings rather than shown in a disabled state.
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Seeing your evolution dashboard (Priority: P1)
22	
23	The user opens the Settings screen and sees, at a glance, a chart of how their recorded entries have built up over time, plus a short AI-written paragraph that puts that pattern into words. Whether they have no entries yet, just one, or a long history, the screen always shows something coherent rather than breaking or looking empty by accident.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF09 — without a correctly rendering chart and narrative, the feature does not exist. **Scope: aggregation and rendering only — the quality of the AI-written narrative text is never evaluated.**
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by opening Settings for accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries respectively, and confirming each renders its own distinct, non-crashing state with the correct chart and text.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** the user has zero entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a light-gray placeholder chart icon (no chart) and the text "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", with no AI narrative paragraph shown or requested.
32	2. **Given** the user has exactly one entry, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a single small bar and the text "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", with no AI narrative paragraph attempted.
33	3. **Given** the user has more than thirty entries, **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows a multi-bar ochre chart (aggregated into the chart's fixed number of buckets) and, once it loads, an AI-written summary paragraph describing the pattern.
34	4. **Given** the chart has loaded successfully for an account with data, **When** the AI narrative call fails or times out, **Then** the chart remains visible and correct, and the narrative area shows a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message rather than staying blank or showing the empty-history copy.
35	5. **Given** the user created a new entry in another screen since Settings was last open, **When** they open Settings again, **Then** the dashboard reflects the new entry in its aggregate — recomputed fresh, not read from a stale result of the previous visit.
36	6. **Given** the user has more than one entry but not enough to populate every one of the chart's ten bars (e.g. 5 or 15 entries), **When** they open Settings, **Then** the dashboard shows the same multi-bar chart and narrative behavior as the "more than thirty entries" case, just with fewer of the ten bars populated — not the single-bar "Ainda é cedo..." message and not a separate, undefined state.
37	
38	---
39	
40	### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)
41	
42	A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.
43	
44	**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.
45	
46	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.
47	
48	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
49	
50	1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
51	2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
52	3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
53	4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.
54	
55	---
56	
57	### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)
58	
59	From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.
60	
61	**Why this priority**: Explicitly named in the feature's scope ("the profile and account actions that live on it") but individually lower risk and lower complexity than the dashboard or account deletion.
62	
63	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by editing the display name and confirming it persists after reopening the app, flipping the biometric toggle and confirming it is saved, and tapping "Sair" and confirming the session ends.
64	
65	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
66	
67	1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** the screen loads, **Then** it shows an initials avatar (52px), the current display name and email, and the editable-name control as a pencil icon.
68	2. **Given** the user taps the pencil icon next to their name, **When** the name field becomes editable, **Then** the pencil icon becomes a check icon and the email remains read-only (not editable) throughout.
69	3. **Given** the user edits their name to a valid value (1–80 characters) and taps the check icon, **When** the save request succeeds, **Then** the field returns to display mode showing the new name, and the new name is still shown after the app is restarted.
70	4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
71	5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).
72	6. **Given** the user taps "Sair", **When** the sign-out request completes (or fails), **Then** the local session is cleared either way, and the user lands at the app's authentication entry point with no residual access to their data.
73	
74	---
75	
76	### Edge Cases
77	
78	- The GET /dashboard/aggregate call itself fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), independent of the narrative call: the dashboard shows a clear, non-crashing error state for the chart area (distinct from the "zero entries" empty state) with a way to retry, and no narrative is requested until the aggregate succeeds.
79	- The session expires while Settings is open (dashboard loading, name being edited, or a confirmation dialog open): the existing expired-session handling (established by F000, continued by RF07) takes over exactly as it does elsewhere; re-authenticating returns the user to Settings with the dashboard, profile, and any in-progress edit reasonably re-requested, not silently lost.
80	- The user double-taps "Apagar tudo" or "Sair" before the first request resolves: this does not fire a second concurrent delete/logout request.
81	- The device has no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled: the toggle row is hidden entirely (not shown in a disabled state), rather than letting the user "turn on" something the device cannot perform.
82	- The user submits an empty name or one over 80 characters: the save is blocked client-side with a clear validation message, no request is sent, and the field stays in edit mode.
83	- Opening Settings, viewing the dashboard, editing the profile, or opening (and cancelling) the delete-confirmation dialog does not alter any other screen's state — My Records' list/filters, chat sessions, or action plans are untouched by this unit.
84	
85	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
86	
87	### Functional Requirements
88	
89	- **FR-001**: Opening Settings MUST request `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and `GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, so that a narrative failure or delay never blocks the chart from rendering with the aggregate data it already has.
90	- **FR-002**: The dashboard MUST request and render a single, fixed period and MUST NOT present a user-facing control to switch between periods in this unit — the prototype shows no such control, and only the fixed period's acceptance scenarios (zero / one / more than thirty entries) are in scope.
91	- **FR-003**: When the aggregate for the active period contains zero entries, the dashboard MUST show the light-gray placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", and MUST NOT request or show the narrative.
92	- **FR-004**: When the aggregate contains exactly one entry, the dashboard MUST show a single small bar and "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", and MUST NOT request or show the narrative.
93	- **FR-005**: When the aggregate contains two or more entries, the dashboard MUST render the multi-bar chart using whatever of the chart's ten bars the aggregate's buckets populate — naturally partial for a small count, fully populated once an account has enough history (the "more than thirty entries" scenario is the seed count chosen to reliably exercise a fully-populated chart, not a distinct functional threshold) — and MUST request the narrative, showing it once it resolves.
94	- **FR-006**: If the narrative call fails, times out, or returns an error after the chart has already rendered successfully, the dashboard MUST show a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message in the narrative's place, without affecting the already-rendered chart and without being confused with the zero-entries empty state.
95	- **FR-007**: If the aggregate call itself fails, the dashboard MUST show a clear, non-crashing, retryable error state for the chart area, distinct from the zero-entries state, and MUST NOT request the narrative until the aggregate succeeds.
96	- **FR-008**: The dashboard MUST be recomputed from a fresh backend call every time Settings is opened, never served from a result cached from a previous visit, so that an entry created elsewhere is reflected the next time Settings is opened.
97	- **FR-009**: Settings MUST display the account's initials avatar, current display name, and current email (read-only) — email MUST NOT be editable in this unit, since `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no email field and rejects attempts to change it.
98	- **FR-010**: Settings MUST let the user edit their display name through an inline pencil-to-check control; saving MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `displayName` (1–80 characters) and MUST update the locally displayed/cached name on success.
99	- **FR-011**: A client-side validation MUST block submitting an empty name or one longer than 80 characters, with no backend call made and the field left in edit mode with an inline error.
100	- **FR-012**: If the name save fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the field MUST remain in edit mode with the user's typed value intact, show a clear retryable error, and MUST NOT silently revert or discard the typed text.
101	- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, Settings MUST offer a toggle reflecting the account's current `biometricEnabled` preference and MUST let the user change it; changing it MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `biometricEnabled` value, continuing the account-settings read/write path RF03 already established for this same flag. On a device with no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled, the toggle row MUST be hidden entirely rather than shown in a disabled state.
102	- **FR-014**: If the biometric toggle save fails, the toggle MUST revert to its last-confirmed state and show a clear, retryable error, rather than appearing to succeed.
103	- **FR-015**: This unit MUST NOT build the AI persona selector ("Analítico"/"Empático"/"Socrático") or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2), even though `PATCH /account/settings` also carries a `persona` field for that extension.
104	- **FR-016**: Settings MUST offer a "Sair" action that calls `POST /auth/logout` and, regardless of whether that call succeeds or fails, MUST clear the local session and any cached account/profile state and return the user to the app's authentication entry point, with no dedicated "signed out" success screen.
105	- **FR-017**: Settings MUST offer an "Apagar conta" action (styled as destructive/red) that opens a confirmation dialog matching the prototype — red title "Apagar sua conta?", text stating the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button — and MUST NOT call the delete endpoint before this dialog is explicitly confirmed.
106	- **FR-018**: Confirming the dialog MUST call `DELETE /account` with the backend-required `confirmation: "DELETE"` value supplied by the app itself (the user is not asked to type the word "DELETE"; the dialog's own destructive button tap is the explicit confirmation, matching the prototype's two-button dialog with no text field).
107	- **FR-019**: On a successful account deletion, the app MUST clear all local session, cached account/profile, and any other locally held user data, and return the user to the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own — mirroring FR-016's logout behavior.
108	- **FR-020**: If the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the account MUST remain intact, the dialog MUST show a clear retryable error, and MUST NOT report success.
109	- **FR-021**: Cancelling the delete-confirmation dialog MUST dismiss it without any backend call and without altering any Settings state (dashboard, profile fields, or toggle values).
110	- **FR-022**: Repeated taps on "Sair" or "Apagar tudo" before a prior request for the same action resolves MUST NOT fire a second concurrent request.
111	- **FR-023**: If the session expires while Settings is open, the existing expired-session handling (F000, continued by RF07) MUST take over exactly as elsewhere, and re-authenticating MUST return the user to a Settings screen that re-requests the dashboard and profile data rather than showing stale or broken state.
112	- **FR-024**: This unit MUST NOT implement functionality belonging to units later than RF09 in the build order; MUST NOT implement any extension feature (requirements, section 2) beyond what FR-015 already excludes; and MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
113	
114	### Key Entities
115	
116	- **Dashboard Aggregate**: The chart data for one period — a set of date-bucketed counts (split by entry source: manual/audio/photo/chat) plus totals. Always returns a well-formed (possibly all-zero) result rather than an error for an account with no entries; recomputed fresh on every Settings visit, never persisted locally across visits.
117	- **Dashboard Narrative**: An independently-fetched, AI-generated paragraph describing the aggregate's pattern for the same period. Can succeed, fail, or be skipped (zero/one-entry scenarios) independently of whether the aggregate itself loaded successfully.
118	- **Account Profile**: The user's editable identity on this screen — display name (editable), email (read-only), and the biometric-unlock preference (editable, shared with RF03). Since the backend only ever returns this profile as the response of a successful `PATCH /account/settings` call — there is no endpoint to read it standalone — the app treats the most recent successful write (from this unit or from RF03's first-time setup) as the locally held source of truth for what this screen displays, defaulting sensibly (e.g., name derived from email) for an account that has never had a successful write.
119	- **Account Deletion**: A one-way, irreversible action with no corresponding entity afterward — it ends the account and every row tied to it (RNF05), including the signed-in session itself.
120	
121	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
122	
123	### Measurable Outcomes
124	
125	- **SC-001**: Across accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries, the dashboard renders the correct dedicated state in 100% of cases with zero crashes and zero mixed-up states (e.g., the empty-history message never appears alongside chart data).
126	- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases where the chart data itself loaded successfully, the chart remains fully visible and correct, with a distinct, clear explanation shown only in the narrative's place.
127	- **SC-003**: 100% of confirmed account-deletion attempts that succeed on the backend leave the device with no retained local session, cached profile, or other user data, and no path back into the account without creating a new one.
128	- **SC-004**: Zero account deletions occur without the user explicitly reaching and confirming the destructive dialog — cancelling or dismissing it never results in a deleted account.
129	- **SC-005**: A display-name edit that succeeds is still showing the new value after the app is fully restarted, in 100% of tested cases.
130	- **SC-006**: Signing out, from any state the screen can be in, always results in the user reaching the authentication entry point with no residual access, in 100% of tested cases.
131	
132	## Assumptions
133	
134	- **Dashboard period**: The dashboard requests a single, fixed period rather than exposing a period-switching control, since neither the prototype's four Settings states nor its component library describes any period selector, tab, or chip for this screen — only the entry-count-driven states (zero / one / more-than-thirty) are depicted. The backend's `period` enum (`7d`/`30d`/`90d`/`all`) exists independently of this UI decision; this unit sends one fixed value (`all`, so the "more than thirty entries" scenario and the cache-invalidation acceptance criterion are both naturally satisfiable from the user's full history) and does not expose the other three values as a feature of this unit.
135	- **No endpoint to read the current profile**: `GET /auth/session` returns only `id` and `email`; the only way to learn `displayName`, `persona`, or `biometricEnabled` is the response body of a successful `PATCH /account/settings` call. This unit treats the most recent such response (including ones written by RF03's first-time biometric setup) as the locally cached source of truth for what Settings displays, with a sensible default (e.g., a name derived from the email's local part) for an account whose profile has never been successfully written.
136	- **Email is read-only despite the prototype's pencil icon**: The prototype extract describes "editable name/e-mail" with a shared pencil-to-check control, but the frozen API contract's `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no `email` field and explicitly rejects email changes. Per the requirements document's own rule ("where this differs from the API contract, the contract prevails"), this unit treats only the display name as editable and shows the email as plain, read-only text.
137	- **No typed "DELETE" confirmation text field**: The backend requires the literal request field `confirmation: "DELETE"`, but the prototype's confirmation dialog shows only a title, explanatory text, and two buttons — no text input. This unit treats the destructive button tap itself as the required explicit confirmation and supplies the literal value in the request automatically, without asking the user to type anything.
138	- **Where "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" land**: The prototype extract states both actions return to the "Biometria" screen with no dedicated success screen of their own. Since both actions end with no stored session, and F000 already routes a device with no stored session to the login/sign-up screen on next launch, this unit treats "the app's authentication entry point" as whatever F000/RF03 already resolve that case to (the vault screen if a device-level PIN/biometric flow applies with no session, falling through to login otherwise) rather than building a separate destination.
139	- **Biometric toggle is in scope, persona is not**: RF03's own specification explicitly defers the biometric on/off toggle (outside of first-time setup) to "the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit." The persona selector, by contrast, is explicitly listed as a non-implemented extension feature (requirements, section 2) even though both preferences share the same `PATCH /account/settings` endpoint.
140	- **Chart's fixed bucket count and bucketing algorithm**: The chart always has ten bars (the prototype's reference mock). For the fixed `all` period — which can span anywhere from a few days to years of account history — this unit divides the account's full date range (date of the first entry through today) into ten roughly-equal time slices and sums the aggregate's per-date `count` values falling within each slice to produce each bar's value. An account whose history is short or clustered naturally produces a chart with some empty bars rather than this being treated as a defect; this unit does not need to support an arbitrary, unbounded number of visible bars.
141	- **Multi-bar chart applies to any count above one, not only "more than thirty"**: FR-005's chart-and-narrative state is not gated on a literal minimum entry count beyond "two or more" — an account with, say, 5 or 15 entries gets the same multi-bar chart (naturally sparser) and narrative request as a 30+ entry account. The "more than thirty entries" acceptance scenario exists only to guarantee a chart where every one of the ten bars is populated, for a clean, unambiguous test case — not because counts between two and thirty are a separate, unspecified state.
142

### User Story 2 - Deleting your account for good (Priority: P1)

A user who wants to leave can permanently erase their account and every piece of data tied to it, with a clear, hard-to-misclick warning first, and no way to undo it afterward.

**Why this priority**: Required by RNF05 (LGPD hard delete) — a legal and trust-critical capability, not a convenience feature. Getting this wrong (deleting too little, deleting by accident, or appearing to delete without really doing so) is a compliance and trust failure, not just a bug.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by tapping "Apagar conta", confirming through the destructive dialog, and verifying the account can no longer log in and the Settings screen is left entirely (no residual session), independent of any other screen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** they tap "Apagar conta", **Then** a centered confirmation dialog appears with a red title ("Apagar sua conta?"), explanatory text that the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button.
2. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Cancelar", **Then** the dialog closes, no backend call is made, and Settings is otherwise unaffected.
3. **Given** the confirmation dialog is open, **When** the user taps "Apagar tudo", **Then** the app requests the account's permanent deletion, and on success clears all local session and account state and leaves the user at the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own.
4. **Given** the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the account is left intact, the user sees a clear error, and can retry — the dialog does not falsely report success.

---

### User Story 3 - Signing out and managing your profile (Priority: P2)

From the same screen, the user can see their profile, rename themselves, flip the Face ID/Touch ID unlock preference on or off, and sign out — all lower-stakes, everyday actions compared to Stories 1 and 2.

**Why this priority**: Explicitly named in the feature's scope ("the profile and account actions that live on it") but individually lower risk and lower complexity than the dashboard or account deletion.

**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by editing the display name and confirming it persists after reopening the app, flipping the biometric toggle and confirming it is saved, and tapping "Sair" and confirming the session ends.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the user is on Settings, **When** the screen loads, **Then** it shows an initials avatar (52px), the current display name and email, and the editable-name control as a pencil icon.
2. **Given** the user taps the pencil icon next to their name, **When** the name field becomes editable, **Then** the pencil icon becomes a check icon and the email remains read-only (not editable) throughout.
3. **Given** the user edits their name to a valid value (1–80 characters) and taps the check icon, **When** the save request succeeds, **Then** the field returns to display mode showing the new name, and the new name is still shown after the app is restarted.
4. **Given** the save request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), **When** the failure is reported, **Then** the field stays in edit mode with the user's typed text intact, a clear error is shown, and the user can retry without re-typing.
5. **Given** the device supports biometrics, **When** the user flips the "Face ID/Touch ID" toggle on Settings, **Then** the app saves the new preference, and the toggle reflects the saved state (or reverts with an error if the save fails).
6. **Given** the user taps "Sair", **When** the sign-out request completes (or fails), **Then** the local session is cleared either way, and the user lands at the app's authentication entry point with no residual access to their data.

---

### Edge Cases

- The GET /dashboard/aggregate call itself fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), independent of the narrative call: the dashboard shows a clear, non-crashing error state for the chart area (distinct from the "zero entries" empty state) with a way to retry, and no narrative is requested until the aggregate succeeds.
- The session expires while Settings is open (dashboard loading, name being edited, or a confirmation dialog open): the existing expired-session handling (established by F000, continued by RF07) takes over exactly as it does elsewhere; re-authenticating returns the user to Settings with the dashboard, profile, and any in-progress edit reasonably re-requested, not silently lost.
- The user double-taps "Apagar tudo" or "Sair" before the first request resolves: this does not fire a second concurrent delete/logout request.
- The device has no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled: the toggle row is hidden entirely (not shown in a disabled state), rather than letting the user "turn on" something the device cannot perform.
- The user submits an empty name or one over 80 characters: the save is blocked client-side with a clear validation message, no request is sent, and the field stays in edit mode.
- Opening Settings, viewing the dashboard, editing the profile, or opening (and cancelling) the delete-confirmation dialog does not alter any other screen's state — My Records' list/filters, chat sessions, or action plans are untouched by this unit.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Opening Settings MUST request `GET /dashboard/aggregate` and `GET /dashboard/narrative` as two independent calls, so that a narrative failure or delay never blocks the chart from rendering with the aggregate data it already has.
- **FR-002**: The dashboard MUST request and render a single, fixed period and MUST NOT present a user-facing control to switch between periods in this unit — the prototype shows no such control, and only the fixed period's acceptance scenarios (zero / one / more than thirty entries) are in scope.
- **FR-003**: When the aggregate for the active period contains zero entries, the dashboard MUST show the light-gray placeholder chart icon and "Comece a registrar para ver sua evolução aqui", and MUST NOT request or show the narrative.
- **FR-004**: When the aggregate contains exactly one entry, the dashboard MUST show a single small bar and "Ainda é cedo pra ver um padrão — volte em alguns dias.", and MUST NOT request or show the narrative.
- **FR-005**: When the aggregate contains two or more entries, the dashboard MUST render the multi-bar chart using whatever of the chart's ten bars the aggregate's buckets populate — naturally partial for a small count, fully populated once an account has enough history (the "more than thirty entries" scenario is the seed count chosen to reliably exercise a fully-populated chart, not a distinct functional threshold) — and MUST request the narrative, showing it once it resolves.
- **FR-006**: If the narrative call fails, times out, or returns an error after the chart has already rendered successfully, the dashboard MUST show a distinct "narrativa indisponível" message in the narrative's place, without affecting the already-rendered chart and without being confused with the zero-entries empty state.
- **FR-007**: If the aggregate call itself fails, the dashboard MUST show a clear, non-crashing, retryable error state for the chart area, distinct from the zero-entries state, and MUST NOT request the narrative until the aggregate succeeds.
- **FR-008**: The dashboard MUST be recomputed from a fresh backend call every time Settings is opened, never served from a result cached from a previous visit, so that an entry created elsewhere is reflected the next time Settings is opened.
- **FR-009**: Settings MUST display the account's initials avatar, current display name, and current email (read-only) — email MUST NOT be editable in this unit, since `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no email field and rejects attempts to change it.
- **FR-010**: Settings MUST let the user edit their display name through an inline pencil-to-check control; saving MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `displayName` (1–80 characters) and MUST update the locally displayed/cached name on success.
- **FR-011**: A client-side validation MUST block submitting an empty name or one longer than 80 characters, with no backend call made and the field left in edit mode with an inline error.
- **FR-012**: If the name save fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the field MUST remain in edit mode with the user's typed value intact, show a clear retryable error, and MUST NOT silently revert or discard the typed text.
- **FR-013**: On a device where biometrics are available, Settings MUST offer a toggle reflecting the account's current `biometricEnabled` preference and MUST let the user change it; changing it MUST call `PATCH /account/settings` with the new `biometricEnabled` value, continuing the account-settings read/write path RF03 already established for this same flag. On a device with no biometric hardware or nothing enrolled, the toggle row MUST be hidden entirely rather than shown in a disabled state.
- **FR-014**: If the biometric toggle save fails, the toggle MUST revert to its last-confirmed state and show a clear, retryable error, rather than appearing to succeed.
- **FR-015**: This unit MUST NOT build the AI persona selector ("Analítico"/"Empático"/"Socrático") or any other extension feature (requirements, section 2), even though `PATCH /account/settings` also carries a `persona` field for that extension.
- **FR-016**: Settings MUST offer a "Sair" action that calls `POST /auth/logout` and, regardless of whether that call succeeds or fails, MUST clear the local session and any cached account/profile state and return the user to the app's authentication entry point, with no dedicated "signed out" success screen.
- **FR-017**: Settings MUST offer an "Apagar conta" action (styled as destructive/red) that opens a confirmation dialog matching the prototype — red title "Apagar sua conta?", text stating the action is permanent and irreversible, a red "Apagar tudo" button, and an outline "Cancelar" button — and MUST NOT call the delete endpoint before this dialog is explicitly confirmed.
- **FR-018**: Confirming the dialog MUST call `DELETE /account` with the backend-required `confirmation: "DELETE"` value supplied by the app itself (the user is not asked to type the word "DELETE"; the dialog's own destructive button tap is the explicit confirmation, matching the prototype's two-button dialog with no text field).
- **FR-019**: On a successful account deletion, the app MUST clear all local session, cached account/profile, and any other locally held user data, and return the user to the app's authentication entry point, with no "account deleted" success screen of its own — mirroring FR-016's logout behavior.
- **FR-020**: If the deletion request fails (timeout, no connection, malformed response), the account MUST remain intact, the dialog MUST show a clear retryable error, and MUST NOT report success.
- **FR-021**: Cancelling the delete-confirmation dialog MUST dismiss it without any backend call and without altering any Settings state (dashboard, profile fields, or toggle values).
- **FR-022**: Repeated taps on "Sair" or "Apagar tudo" before a prior request for the same action resolves MUST NOT fire a second concurrent request.
- **FR-023**: If the session expires while Settings is open, the existing expired-session handling (F000, continued by RF07) MUST take over exactly as elsewhere, and re-authenticating MUST return the user to a Settings screen that re-requests the dashboard and profile data rather than showing stale or broken state.
- **FR-024**: This unit MUST NOT implement functionality belonging to units later than RF09 in the build order; MUST NOT implement any extension feature (requirements, section 2) beyond what FR-015 already excludes; and MUST NOT modify the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.

### Key Entities

- **Dashboard Aggregate**: The chart data for one period — a set of date-bucketed counts (split by entry source: manual/audio/photo/chat) plus totals. Always returns a well-formed (possibly all-zero) result rather than an error for an account with no entries; recomputed fresh on every Settings visit, never persisted locally across visits.
- **Dashboard Narrative**: An independently-fetched, AI-generated paragraph describing the aggregate's pattern for the same period. Can succeed, fail, or be skipped (zero/one-entry scenarios) independently of whether the aggregate itself loaded successfully.
- **Account Profile**: The user's editable identity on this screen — display name (editable), email (read-only), and the biometric-unlock preference (editable, shared with RF03). Since the backend only ever returns this profile as the response of a successful `PATCH /account/settings` call — there is no endpoint to read it standalone — the app treats the most recent successful write (from this unit or from RF03's first-time setup) as the locally held source of truth for what this screen displays, defaulting sensibly (e.g., name derived from email) for an account that has never had a successful write.
- **Account Deletion**: A one-way, irreversible action with no corresponding entity afterward — it ends the account and every row tied to it (RNF05), including the signed-in session itself.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Across accounts seeded with zero, one, and more than thirty entries, the dashboard renders the correct dedicated state in 100% of cases with zero crashes and zero mixed-up states (e.g., the empty-history message never appears alongside chart data).
- **SC-002**: In 100% of forced narrative-failure cases where the chart data itself loaded successfully, the chart remains fully visible and correct, with a distinct, clear explanation shown only in the narrative's place.
- **SC-003**: 100% of confirmed account-deletion attempts that succeed on the backend leave the device with no retained local session, cached profile, or other user data, and no path back into the account without creating a new one.
- **SC-004**: Zero account deletions occur without the user explicitly reaching and confirming the destructive dialog — cancelling or dismissing it never results in a deleted account.
- **SC-005**: A display-name edit that succeeds is still showing the new value after the app is fully restarted, in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-006**: Signing out, from any state the screen can be in, always results in the user reaching the authentication entry point with no residual access, in 100% of tested cases.

## Assumptions

- **Dashboard period**: The dashboard requests a single, fixed period rather than exposing a period-switching control, since neither the prototype's four Settings states nor its component library describes any period selector, tab, or chip for this screen — only the entry-count-driven states (zero / one / more-than-thirty) are depicted. The backend's `period` enum (`7d`/`30d`/`90d`/`all`) exists independently of this UI decision; this unit sends one fixed value (`all`, so the "more than thirty entries" scenario and the cache-invalidation acceptance criterion are both naturally satisfiable from the user's full history) and does not expose the other three values as a feature of this unit.
- **No endpoint to read the current profile**: `GET /auth/session` returns only `id` and `email`; the only way to learn `displayName`, `persona`, or `biometricEnabled` is the response body of a successful `PATCH /account/settings` call. This unit treats the most recent such response (including ones written by RF03's first-time biometric setup) as the locally cached source of truth for what Settings displays, with a sensible default (e.g., a name derived from the email's local part) for an account whose profile has never been successfully written.
- **Email is read-only despite the prototype's pencil icon**: The prototype extract describes "editable name/e-mail" with a shared pencil-to-check control, but the frozen API contract's `PATCH /account/settings` accepts no `email` field and explicitly rejects email changes. Per the requirements document's own rule ("where this differs from the API contract, the contract prevails"), this unit treats only the display name as editable and shows the email as plain, read-only text.
- **No typed "DELETE" confirmation text field**: The backend requires the literal request field `confirmation: "DELETE"`, but the prototype's confirmation dialog shows only a title, explanatory text, and two buttons — no text input. This unit treats the destructive button tap itself as the required explicit confirmation and supplies the literal value in the request automatically, without asking the user to type anything.
- **Where "Sair" and "Apagar tudo" land**: The prototype extract states both actions return to the "Biometria" screen with no dedicated success screen of their own. Since both actions end with no stored session, and F000 already routes a device with no stored session to the login/sign-up screen on next launch, this unit treats "the app's authentication entry point" as whatever F000/RF03 already resolve that case to (the vault screen if a device-level PIN/biometric flow applies with no session, falling through to login otherwise) rather than building a separate destination.
- **Biometric toggle is in scope, persona is not**: RF03's own specification explicitly defers the biometric on/off toggle (outside of first-time setup) to "the Settings screen built by the RF09 unit." The persona selector, by contrast, is explicitly listed as a non-implemented extension feature (requirements, section 2) even though both preferences share the same `PATCH /account/settings` endpoint.
- **Chart's fixed bucket count and bucketing algorithm**: The chart always has ten bars (the prototype's reference mock). For the fixed `all` period — which can span anywhere from a few days to years of account history — this unit divides the account's full date range (date of the first entry through today) into ten roughly-equal time slices and sums the aggregate's per-date `count` values falling within each slice to produce each bar's value. An account whose history is short or clustered naturally produces a chart with some empty bars rather than this being treated as a defect; this unit does not need to support an arbitrary, unbounded number of visible bars.
- **Multi-bar chart applies to any count above one, not only "more than thirty"**: FR-005's chart-and-narrative state is not gated on a literal minimum entry count beyond "two or more" — an account with, say, 5 or 15 entries gets the same multi-bar chart (naturally sparser) and narrative request as a 30+ entry account. The "more than thirty entries" acceptance scenario exists only to guarantee a chart where every one of the ten bars is populated, for a clean, unambiguous test case — not because counts between two and thirty are a separate, unspecified state.
